arxiv-2111-14441.title: Sub-dimensional Mardia measures of multivariate skewness and kurtosis
arxiv-2111-14441.creator: Joydeep Chowdhury, Subhajit Dutta, Reinaldo B. Arellano-Valle, Marc G. Genton
arxiv-2111-14441.description: Abstract The Mardia measures of multivariate skewness and kurtosis summarize the respective characteristics of a multivariate distribution with two numbers. However, these measures do not reflect the sub-dimensional features of the distribution. Consequently, testing procedures based on these measures may fail to detect skewness or kurtosis present in a sub-dimension of the multivariate distribution.

arxiv-2209-04527.title: Control of magnetic states and spin interactions in bilayer CrCl 3 with strain and electric fields: An ab initio study
arxiv-2209-04527.creator: Ali Ebrahimian, Anna Dyrdał, Alireza Qaiumzadeh
arxiv-2209-04527.description: Abstract Using ab initio density functional theory (DFT), we demonstrated the possibility of controlling the magnetic ground-state properties of bilayer CrCl 3 by means of mechanical strains and electric fields. In principle, we investigated the influence of these two fields on parameters describing the spin Hamiltonian of the system.

arxiv-2306-14515.title: Optimizing Kernel-Target Alignment for cloud detection in multispectral satellite images
arxiv-2306-14515.creator: Artur Miroszewski 1 , Jakub Mielczarek 1 , Filip Szczepanek 1 , Grzegorz Czelusta 1 , Bartosz Grabowski 2 , Bertrand Le Saux 3 , and Jakub Nalepa 2,4
arxiv-2306-14515.description: Abstract The optimization of Kernel-Target Alignment (TA) has been recently proposed as a way to reduce the number of hardware resources in quantum classifiers. It allows to exchange highly expressive and costly circuits to moderate size, task oriented ones. In this work we propose a simple toy model to study the optimization landscape of the Kernel-Target Alignment.

arxiv-2310-03811.title: Catalog variance of testing general relativity with gravitational-wave data
arxiv-2310-03811.creator: Costantino Pacilio, Davide Gerosa, Swetha Bhagwat
arxiv-2310-03811.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Costantino Pacilio, Davide Gerosa, Swetha Bhagwat. Combining multiple gravitational-wave observations allows for stringent tests of general relativity, targeting effects that would otherwise be undetectable using single-event analyses. We highlight how the finite size of the observed catalog induces a significant source of variance. If not appropriately accounted for, general relativity can be excluded with arbitrarily large credibility even if it is the underlying theory of gravity. This effect is generic and holds for arbitrarily large catalogs.

arxiv-2403-19011.title: Sequential Inference of Hospitalization Electronic Health Records Using Probabilistic Models
arxiv-2403-19011.creator: Alan D. Kaplan and Priyadip Ray, John D. Greene and Vincent X. Liu
arxiv-2403-19011.description: Abstract In the dynamic hospital setting, decision support can be a valuable tool for improving patient outcomes. Data-driven inference of future outcomes is challenging in this dynamic setting, where long sequences such as laboratory tests and medications are updated frequently. This is due in part to heterogeneity of data types and mixed-sequence types contained in variable length sequences.

arxiv-2406-12594.title: On optimizing Inband Telemetry systems for accurate latency-based service deployments
arxiv-2406-12594.creator: Nataliia Koneva 1 , Alfonso Sánchez-Macián 1 , José Alberto Hernández 1 , Ó. González de Dios 2
arxiv-2406-12594.description: Abstract The power of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence algorithms based on collected datasets, along with the programmability and flexibility provided by Software Defined Networking can provide the building blocks for constructing the so-called Zero-Touch Network and Service Management systems. However, the fuel towards this goal relies on the availability of sufficient and good-quality data collected from measurements and telemetry.

arxiv-2409-16391.title: Patch-Based Contrastive Learning and Memory Consolidation for Online Unsupervised Continual Learning
arxiv-2409-16391.creator: Cameron Taylor cameron.taylor@gatech.edu, Vassilis Vassiliades v.vassiliades@cyens.org.cy, Constantine Dovrolis constantine@gatech.edu
arxiv-2409-16391.description: Abstract We focus on a relatively unexplored learning paradigm known as Online Unsupervised Continual Learning (O-UCL), where an agent receives a non-stationary, unlabeled data stream and progressively learns to identify an increasing number of classes. This paradigm is designed to model real-world applications where encountering novelty is the norm, such as exploring a terrain with several unknown and time-varying entities.

arxiv-2411-08661.title: Energy Optimal Traversal Between Hover Waypoints for Lift+Cruise Electric Powered Aircraft
arxiv-2411-08661.creator: Ella Atkins
arxiv-2411-08661.description: Abstract Advanced Air Mobility aircraft require energy efficient flight plans to be economically viable. This paper defines minimum energy direct trajectories between waypoints for Lift+Cruise electric Vertical Take-Off and Landing (eVTOL) aircraft. Energy consumption is optimized over accelerated and cruise flight profiles with consideration of mode transitions.

arxiv-2505-08591.title: An extreme value method to study decadal hurricane wind trends
arxiv-2505-08591.creator: Alexandre Payez, \aff a Ad Stoffelen, \aff a Cees de Valk, \aff a, Rianne Giesen \aff a
arxiv-2505-08591.description: Abstract This paper presents a method developed using techniques from extreme value theory to estimate smooth wind-speed percentiles, allowing us to consider more extreme wind speeds while being less sensitive to the noise that stems from the scarcity of extreme data.

arxiv-2507-13157.title: Multi-population GAN Training: Analyzing Co-Evolutionary Algorithms CCS: Computing methodologies Unsupervised learning CCS: Computing methodologies Bio-inspired approaches CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
arxiv-2507-13157.creator: Walter P. Casas, Jamal Toutouh
arxiv-2507-13157.description: Abstract . Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are powerful generative models but remain challenging to train due to pathologies such as mode collapse and instability. Recent research has explored coevolutionary approaches, in which populations of generators and discriminators are evolved, as a promising solution.

arxiv-2507-19708.title: Traverso’s Isogeny Conjecture for Some Unitary p -Divisible Groups
arxiv-2507-19708.creator: Emerald Andrews, Deewang Bhamidipati, Maria Fox, Heidi Goodson, Steven R. Groen, Sandra Nair
arxiv-2507-19708.description: Abstract . The isogeny cutoff of a p p -divisible group X X (defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p p ) measures the amount of p p -torsion necessary to determine its isogeny class. The minimal height of X X measures its distance to the closest minimal p p -divisible group (in the sense of Oort).

merivale-romans-empire-vol-1.description: Merivale's Victorian classic of imperial Rome, Vol. 1 — Augustus and Tiberius.

plos-pone-0008915.creator: Mark P. Little, Wolfgang F. Heidenreich, Guangquan Li
plos-pone-0008915.description: PLOS ONE research article. Models for complex biological systems may involve a large number of parameters. It may well be that some of these parameters cannot be derived from observed data via regression techniques. Such parameters are said to be unidentifiable, the remaining parameters being identifiable.

pmc-11435103.creator: Lei Yang, Luqiao Sun, Yuanyuan Sun, Guangwei Qiu, Xiaoguang Fan, Qing Sun, Guang Lu
pmc-11435103.description: Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) offers a promising platform for non-invasive and gentle cell detachment. However, conventional PNIPAM-based substrates often suffer from limitations including limited stability and reduced reusability, which hinder their widespread adoption in biomedical applications. In this study, PNIPAM copolymer films were formed on the surfaces of glass slides or silicon wafers using a two-step film-forming method involving coating and grafting.

pmc-11862279.title: Brain developmental trajectories in offspring of parents with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder
pmc-11862279.creator: N Van Haren
pmc-11862279.description: AbstractEarly diagnosis and intervention are essential for managing and improving long-term outcomes of severe mental illness, highlighting the need for reliable early biomarkers. This longitudinal study explores whether the development of the brain during childhood and adolescence differs between offspring of parents with and without schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.

pmc-12412947.title: International Network of Antibiotic Allergy Nations (iNAAN): Protocol for a type 2 hybrid effectiveness-implementation multicentre prospective cohort and target trial emulation study evaluating penicillin allergy delabeling via direct oral challenge

pmc-12461408.title: Geochemical Characteristics and Oil-Gas Geological Significance of the Cambrian Bituminous Calcite Veins in the Northeast Margin of Ordos Basin, China
pmc-12461408.creator: Wei Chen, Xiaofeng Wang, Wenhui Liu, Dongdong Zhang, Houyong Luo, Xiaofu Li, Xiaoqi Yuan
pmc-12461408.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The bituminous calcite vein in the basin is an important basis for indicating fluid activity, hydrocarbon migration, and evolution. This paper systematically describes the microscopic petrological characteristics of two types of bituminous calcite veins and surrounding rocks from the Cambrian Xuzhuang Formation in Qingshuihe area, northeast margin of Ordos Basin, and their geochemical characteristics were analyzed by X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XRF) content, reflectance R b, inorganic carbon and oxygen isotope composition (δ13Ccarb, δ18Ocarb) and organic carbon isotope composition (δ13Corg).

pmc-12565102.title: Comparative Effects of Adapted Taekwondo Versus Tai Chi on Health Status in Independent Older Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial
pmc-12565102.creator: Tomás Herrera-Valenzuela, Izham Cid-Calfucura, Jordan Hernandez-Martinez, Pablo Valdés-Badilla, José Manuel García-García, Bibiana Calvo-Rico, Cristián Cofre-Bolados, Amaya Pavez-Lizarraga, Verónica Flandes-Vargas, Álvaro Segueida-Lorca, Celso Sánchez-Ramírez
pmc-12565102.description: Background: Taekwondo (TKD) and Tai Chi (TC) are promising interventions for enhancing health and physical function in older people, yet few studies have compared their effects across multiple domains. This study aimed to compare the effects of TKD versus TC on health status in independent older women.

pmc-12649839.title: Evaluating the Performance of Hyperspectral Imaging Endoscopes: Mitigating Parameters Affecting Spectral Accuracy
pmc-12649839.creator: Siavash Mazdeyasna, Mohammed Shahriar Arefin, Andrew Fales, Silas J. Leavesley, T. Joshua Pfefer, Quanzeng Wang
pmc-12649839.description: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is increasingly used in studies for medical applications as it provides both structural and functional information of biological tissue, enhancing diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision-making. Recently, HSI cameras (HSICs) have been integrated with medical endoscopes (HSIEs), capturing hypercube data beyond conventional white light imaging endoscopes. However, there are currently no cleared or approved HSIEs by the U.S.

pmc-12719752.title: Time-warped representational similarity analysis reveals acoustic contributions to musical pleasure are weakly shaped by autonomic neural inputs
pmc-12719752.creator: Vincent KM Cheung, Tamaka Harada, Shu Sakamoto, Shinichi Furuya
pmc-12719752.description: SummaryMost people enjoy music and often use it to regulate their emotions. Although pleasure derived from music-listening has been shown to be mediated by dopaminergic signals in the mesolimbic reward network, its relationship with physiology has been inconsistent. Here, we introduced time-warped representational similarity analysis (twRSA) to directly map dynamic representations of multiple modalities across variable-duration stimuli.

pmc-12772052.title: All providers Better Communication Skills (ABCs) program: protocol for a randomized controlled trial assessing communication training effectiveness with interprofessional clinicians
pmc-12772052.creator: Hsien Seow, Anish K Arora, Daryl Bainbridge, Zhimeng Jia, Leah Steinberg, Nadia Incardona, Oren Levine, Justin J Sanders, Jessica Simon, Amanda Roze des Ordons, Karen Zhang, Jeff Myers
pmc-12772052.description: BackgroundHigh-quality person-centred communication for those living with serious illness benefits patients, families, and health care professionals (HCPs). However, research suggests that HCPs often find it challenging to engage in these discussions. The purpose of this study is to assess the effectiveness of the ‘All providers Better Communication Skills’ (ABCs), an online blended learning program delivered over three months.

pmc-13000710.title: Target-enhanced double-pulse LIBS coupled with feature-fused CNN for mechanistic and interpretable coffee origin authentication
pmc-13000710.creator: Xiaoyong He, Kaiqiang Que, Tingrui Liang, Zhenman Gao, Zenghui Wang, Yufeng Li
pmc-13000710.description: Coffee geographical origin authentication is critical for mitigating economically motivated adulteration, yet rapid trace-element analysis in complex organic matrices remains a significant challenge. This study establishes a novel synergistic framework integrating Potassium-assisted orthogonal Double-Pulse Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (DP-LIBS) with a Feature-Fused CNN for precise coffee traceability.

pmc-13058694.title: Spectroscopic Investigation of Thioacrolein by Variational and Perturbational Approaches
pmc-13058694.creator: Guntram Rauhut
pmc-13058694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The vibrational spectra of trans and cis‐thioacrolein have been studied by 2nd order vibrational perturbation theory (VPT2) and vibrational configuration interaction (VCI) theory. All calculations rely on multilevel potential energy surfaces (PESs) with the highest level being explicitly correlated coupled‐cluster theory including single and double excitation and a perturbational treatment of the triple excitation in combination with an augmented triple‐ζ basis set. Comparisons with experimental data are provided, including a number of predictions for unobserved fundamentals.

pmc-13094063.title: Assessing the non-inferiority of a 10-day compared with a 14-day vonoprazan–amoxicillin dual therapy regimen for H. pylori eradication: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13094063.creator: Azzam Zrineh, Rami Akwan, Muhammad M Elsharkawy, Mostafa Adel T Mahmoud, Hadeel Ayesh, Mazen Momtaz Shehata, Hamza Karmi, Elsayed S Moubarak
pmc-13094063.description: BackgroundHelicobacter pylori infection affects approximately 50% of the global population and remains a major cause of peptic ulcer disease and gastric cancer. Vonoprazan, a novel potassium-competitive acid blocker, has emerged as a promising alternative to proton pump inhibitors in H. pylori eradication regimens. Vonoprazan-amoxicillin dual therapy offers a simplified treatment approach with potentially high eradication rates.

pmc-13124324.title: ERAT combined with electrohydraulic lithotripsy for the treatment of chronic appendicitis with giant fecal stones in the appendix: A case report
pmc-13124324.creator: Chun Gao, Xiang-Xiang Zhu, Wei Wang
pmc-13124324.description: Rationale:Endoscopic retrograde appendicitis therapy (ERAT) has emerged as a minimally invasive treatment option for acute uncomplicated appendicitis. However, its application in chronic appendicitis with giant appendicoliths is rarely reported. Such cases present a significant challenge for ERAT due to the difficult removal of large, impacted fecal stones using conventional techniques.

pmc-13248367.title: Spatially multimodal and multiscale network for representation learning from spatial multi-omics
pmc-13248367.creator: Fengyu Zhang, Cheng Peng
pmc-13248367.description: BackgroundSpatial multi-omics techniques provide powerful tools to decipher tissue architectures in multilayer perspectives, including gene expressions, gene regulations and microenvironments. The multimodal data integration is a critical step in spatial multi-omics data processing involved in many downstream analyses, such as spatial domain clustering.

pmc-13275792.title: Impact of CBD and hemp oil use on drug test results: a systematic review
pmc-13275792.creator: Duygu Yeşim Ovat, Ezgi Bezci, Kemal Balıca, Umut Kırlı, Serap Annette Akgur
pmc-13275792.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHemp-derived products, especially CBD (cannabidiol) oil and hemp oil, have shown a notable increase of use in recent years. CBD oil is a compound derived from the cannabis plant, whilst hemp oil is a product derived from hemp seeds. Trans-Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) in cannabis is responsible for the psychoactive effect, whereas CBD, having the same molecular weight, is a non-psychoactive compound with analgesic, antiepileptic, antibacterial and anti-inflammatory effects.

pmc-13284855.title: Lightweight deep learning for medical imaging using MobileNetV2-based brain pathology classification with Grad-CAM interpretability
pmc-13284855.creator: Mian Usman Sattar, Meznah A. Alamro, Alaeddine Mihoub, Soliman Aljarboa, Moez Krichen
pmc-13284855.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionComputed Tomography (CT) brain scans are crucial for diagnosing various neurological conditions, including tumors, cancer, and aneurysms. CT brain scans are essential for guiding treatment decisions and monitoring disease progression. In this study, we propose a novel framework for brain CT image classification that leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) pre-processing, transfer learning with multiple deep models, and ensemble prediction techniques.

pmc-13362377.title: Association Between Endogenous Ketosis and Risk of Atrial Fibrillation in Intensive Care Versus General Ward Patients: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13362377.creator: Kellina Maduray, Jingquan Zhong

pmc-13375676.title: Rigorous Bound on Hydrodynamic Diffusion for Chaotic Open Spin Chains
pmc-13375676.creator: Dimitrios Ampelogiannis, Benjamin Doyon
pmc-13375676.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The emergence of diffusion is one of the deepest physical phenomena observed in many-body interacting, chaotic systems. But establishing rigorously that correlation functions, say of the spin, expand diffusively, remains one of the most important problems of mathematical physics. We establish for the first time, with Lindbladian evolution, a lower bound on spin diffusion in chaotic, translation-invariant, nearest-neighbor open quantum spin-1/2 chain satisfying a local unitality condition and strong conservation of magnetization.

pmc-13610111.title: Variation in Soil Organic Carbon Along an Altitudinal Gradient Across Different Aspects in the Timberline Zone of the Western Himalaya, India
pmc-13610111.creator: Renu Rawal, Ankur Sharma, Gaurav Mishra, Tanay Barman, Ravi K. Chaturvedi, Lalit M. Tewari
pmc-13610111.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The timberline region of the Western Himalaya is a crucial ecological transition area highly sensitive to climate changes, which significantly influence vegetation patterns, soil formation, and carbon dynamics. This study aimed to investigate the spatial and altitudinal changes in soil organic carbon (SOC) across different topographic orientations and to evaluate machine-learning models for spatial SOC prediction in the timberline ecotone (2100–3300 m) of the Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary.

pmc-13635529.title: Boosting oral bioavailability of taraxasterol via a nanocrystal-mucoadhesive micropatch platform for potent multi-mechanistic protection against drug-induced liver injury
pmc-13635529.creator: Zimin Cai, Huan Zhao, Min Wei, Zhimei Cheng, Huizhou He, Jinzhuan Xu, Shan Xu, Jing Huang, Tingting Xiao, Jianqing Peng, Runbin Sun, Qianming Du, Yi Chen
pmc-13635529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Drug-induced liver injury (DILI) is a serious adverse reaction with limited therapeutic options. Taraxasterol (TAS), a natural triterpenoid with hepatoprotective potential, suffers from poor aqueous solubility and low oral bioavailability, hindering its clinical application. Here, we develop an integrated oral delivery platform comprising TAS nanocrystals (TAS NCs) stabilized by D-α-tocopherol polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS), embedded within chitosan-carbopol polyelectrolyte complex (EPC) micropatches, and encapsulated in enteric-coated capsules (TAS NCs@EPC/CAP).
